written.myAnswer: A computer system includes input and output devices, processing components such as the CPU and memory, storage, and components that connect and communicate between parts, such as the motherboard and system bus.

A computer system is made up of components that work together to process data and carry out instructions. Input devices provide data; the CPU processes it, using memory and storage; and output devices present results. The system’s components communicate with one another, while its objective is to perform tasks and process data.

A computer interacts with its environment through devices and connections. A power supply provides the electrical energy needed to operate it. Users can enter information using devices such as a keyboard or mouse, and the computer processes that input and presents results through an output device. A network connection allows the computer to send and receive data, for example when browsing websites or downloading files. Peripherals such as printers and scanners also let the computer exchange information with its surroundings.

The user selects a file using a mouse or keyboard. The operating system responds to the input and requests the file from storage. The file’s data and instructions are transferred to RAM, and the CPU processes them. The system bus carries data between components, and the display system sends the result to the monitor so the file appears on screen.
